transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t get past this feeling that I’ve failed — as a father, and just as a useful person. It keeps going around in my head, over and over, and I get to the point where I feel like I don’t really deserve much of a future.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to care about?

Yeah. I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, and watching Cubs games with my daughter. Now the trains are just sitting there half-built on the table, and even turning on a game feels… pointless. I just don’t get anything out of it anymore.
Do you find that you feel depressed or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not sure how to measure “most of the day,” exactly. I just know it’s there a lot. The hopeless feeling comes and goes, but it’s been hard to shake lately.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood and loss of interest in things?
It’s been about a month now. It really started after my daughter left for college out of state, and since then I just haven’t felt like myself.

Have you felt this way every day for at least two weeks in a row, and have these feelings ever been so intense that you had trouble functioning normally, like going to work or taking care of daily tasks?

Yes. It’s been every day for more than two weeks. And it’s been bad enough that I’m not keeping up with normal things. Bills are piling up, house projects are just sitting there, and I can’t seem to make myself follow through.

I’ve also stopped seeing the people I used to see at book club or on rides. I don’t feel like I can just brush this off anymore… especially since I started organizing my finances like someone else might need them.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident, even if others around you thought your behavior was out of the ordinary?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember any times where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that, or where people thought I was acting out of character in that way.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before, where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having a stretch like this before, at least not this clearly or for this long.
Have you ever had any other times in your life, before this recent period, where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?
I’m not sure. Looking back, I don’t remember another time before this where it lasted more than two weeks like this. Maybe I had bad weeks here and there, but nothing that stands out the same way.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower or being especially restless. Nothing that stands out to me that way.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, or on the contrary, have you found yourself sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, I’ve been having trouble sleeping. I’ll lie in bed for hours, and the house feels too quiet. Then if I do fall asleep, I wake up around three or four in the morning and can’t get back to sleep. My mind just starts going over everything I’ve messed up.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, focusing, or making decisions lately?

Yes. That’s been a real problem. I used to handle engineering spreadsheets without even thinking much about it, and now I’ll sit there staring at a grocery list or a bill for half an hour and still not know what I’m supposed to do next. It’s like my brain just won’t move.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite — like not wanting to eat at all, or feeling like food just doesn’t taste the same?

Yeah. Most days I don’t really bother making a proper meal. I’ll just… forget to eat until it’s late, and then I only manage something like toast or cereal. I’ve had to tighten my belt lately, so I guess I’m eating less than I realized.
